answer_1.quote: We evaluate our models with both text-based and qualitative metrics that help us to get a nuanced perspective on the performance of the models. For free-form text generation, the NLP community has predominantly used n-gram based metrics. We show results using BLEU-1, ROUGE-L and METEOR.
answer_1.outputs: Generated long-form answers to student questions based on lecture videos

answer_2.quote: We show results using BLEU-1, ROUGE-L and METEOR. We also evaluate using a semantic metric, Entailment Score (ES), which checks the probability of the generated text being entailed within the reference text. We also use LLM-based FactQA Precision and Recall metrics, that give a clearer picture of the notions of correctness and completeness of the generated answers with respect to the ground truth.

answer_3.quote: Hence, we introduce LLM (GPT-4o) based methodologies to get a quantitative estimate of these qualities with the help of Likert Scales.
methods: Likert Scale scoring for Clarity, ECT, and UPT

answer_4.quote: Before we did this, we wanted to ground our interpretations to that of actual students, and validate our Likert Scale. To ensure validity of our LLM-based metrics, we have 2 student annotators (graduates) to annotate the quality scores according to the Likert Scale defined in Table 3, for 320 data points from the test set (50% split of real-world and synthetic).
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were asked to assign scores based on Likert Scales for Clarity, ECT, and UPT with specific scoring criteria defined in Table 3.
